reasons.plausibility: The hypothesis incorrectly attributes the size-dependent melting point depression to increased configurational entropy, whereas the well-known Gibbs-Thomson effect (surface energy) is the dominant mechanism; configurational entropy in HEAs stabilizes the solid solution but does not drive size-dependent melting.
reasons.testability: The proposed test (DSC/TEM of 2-10 nm particles) is feasible and the falsification criterion (no decrease in melting point with decreasing size) is clear and decisive.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis is not useful because it proposes a physically incorrect mechanism (entropy-driven melting) for a well-known phenomenon, offering no new insight into what specifically governs premelting/melting in HEA nanoparticles.
